newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Bardot cleared of racist slur.
newsitem.headline: France's Bardot cleared of racist slur.

text.p: A Paris court on Thursday cleared French former film star Brigitte Bardot of inciting racial hatred by saying that the country was being invaded by sheep-slaughtering Moslems.
The 62-year-old former screen sex symbol turned animal rights activist, cheered by fans and animal lovers, had denied the charges at a December 19 hearing in the case.

The charges, which carry up to a year in prison and a 300,000-franc ($60,000) fine, had been brought by the Movement Against Racism (MRAP), the Human Rights League (LDH) and the League Against Racism and Anti-Semitism (LICRA).

In an outspoken opinion column in the conservative daily Le Figaro last April, the ex-actress who has come under fire for far-right views had denounced as barbarous the ritual slaughter of sheep for the Moslem festival of Aid al-Kebir.
She also criticised, in harsh terms, immigration to France from Moslem countries.
Public prosecutor Marie-Jeanne Vieillard had accused her of denouncing Moslem traditions but had not recommended a particular punishment.
